shared_elements: low-relief carving on a flat dressed stone face
quadruped animal in profile with legs extended
animals stacked one above another in vertical registers
small animal/head in profile below a larger figure
weathered pale stone surface set in an excavated, rubble/earth context
justification: Both show shallow, flattened low relief of profile quadrupeds and smaller animals arranged in stacked vertical registers on the broad face of an upright stone block, with comparable modelling of limbs and outlines that suggests the same carving technique. The clearest difference is density and repertoire: A carries a much richer programme, including a horizontal patterned band, rows of objects at the top, birds, a human-like figure and a snake-like form, whereas B shows only two isolated animal figures on a plainer, more eroded surface.
